policies.title: CPLP, EU, United States and Canada ordinary passports: visa-free entry
policies.summary: Article 25(1)(e) of the published foreign-citizens regime exempts citizens of current CPLP and EU members, the United States and Canada from a visa. This policy maps only the ordinary-passport component of those citizenship categories.
conditions: Law No. 5/2015 names the citizenship groups but does not state an ordinary-passport document subtype, a visitor purpose, or a per-nationality stay period. The current Foreign Ministry brief says waivers are generally 15 days and sometimes 30 or 90 days, but supplies no country-to-duration crosswalk; no duration is asserted here.

A valid recognized travel document, border examination, financial means, accommodation, return/onward evidence, health requirements, security checks and individual admission remain separate. The law and brief do not establish work, residence, study, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Current Foreign Ministry named visa-waiver partners: visa-free entry
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current mobility brief expressly names these additional nationalities within São Tomé and Príncipe's visa-waiver agreements. It is recorded separately because the brief does not publish each underlying agreement or its ordinary-passport detail.
conditions: The current Foreign Ministry brief calls these visa-waiver agreements and says exemptions are generally 15 days, with 30 or 90 days for some states; it does not provide an agreement-by-agreement duration, passport-type, purpose or effective-date crosswalk.

This policy therefore records the named current visa-waiver outcome only for the catalog's ordinary passports, with medium confidence. It does not establish a universal waiver, eVisa, visa on arrival, work, residence, business-only, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, emergency, stateless or other special-document route. Border admission remains discretionary.

unresolved.reason: No current directly competent source reviewed establishes an ordinary São Tomé and Príncipe passport holder's right of return or entry classification. Foreign-citizen visa rules are not enough to infer citizenship access.

The statute's country-citizen categories and its residual third-country-visa waiver do not directly map a Macao SAR passport to a nationality or recognized travel-document route; the live SMF portal has no passport selector.

Law No. 5/2015 only waives a São Tomé and Príncipe visa when this foreign national also holds a valid Schengen or United States visa, has the stated passport validity, and stays no more than 15 days. That document-conditioned exception is not an unconditional nationality baseline. The live SMF e-VisaST/entry-authorization service has no nationality eligibility schedule, so no residual eVisa or advance-visa route is inferred.
